subject: Hosted API latency profile alignment — measurement cadence & carveout request
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@greenbank.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Latency commitments + migration carveouts

Hi Lauren / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we scope procurement we need to firm up the latency SLOs for the hosted API in the contract addendum. Our compliance team is asking for: p50 and p95 targets, how you measure those (sampling cadence, aggregation window), and explicit carveouts during our cloud migration (we expect a 48–72 hour migration window in Q1).

Two asks up front:
- Can Redwood commit to p50/p95 numbers at the tenant level for the production endpoint (GreenBank-prod)?
- Can you describe the measurement window / sampling method and what a temporary tolerance (no-credit exception) during a migration would look like?

We need that language for our SRE and procurement teams by next Tuesday so we can keep the timelines. I attached our internal migration runbook so you can see the expected traffic pattern.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Park
Director, Platform Engineering — GreenBank
ops@greenbank.com
(Attachment: greenbank_migration_runbook_v1.pdf)

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <dpark@greenbank.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency commitments + migration carveouts

On Sun, Nov 7, 2026 at 9:12 AM Daniel Park <dpark@greenbank.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo last week. As we scope procurement we need to firm up the latency SLOs for the hosted API in the contract addendum.

Hi Daniel — appreciate the clear asks and the runbook. High level proposal from Redwood:

- Tenant-level commitments (GreenBank-prod):
  * p50 <= 60 ms
  * p95 <= 320 ms

- Measurement approach:
  * Sampling: continuous per-request percentile calculation with 1-minute buckets; hourly aggregation uses rolling-window percentiles computed from the last 60 1-minute buckets.
  * Reporting: daily and weekly reports; SLA evaluation uses a 24-hour rolling window for breach detection and a 30-day lookback for long-term trend analysis.

- Migration carveout (proposed):
  * Pre-notice: GreenBank provides Redwood a 72-hour migration notice window for planned migration periods.
  * Temporary tolerance: for a timeboxed migration window (up to 72 hours) Redwood will allow up to a 3% transient p95 exceedance without SLA credit, provided Redwood has pre-warmed caches and enabled burst capacity.
  * Evidence: GreenBank must share migration start/end timestamps and traffic patterns; Redwood will correlate metrics and provide a post-migration incident summary.

I attached a draft SLO addendum (greenbank_slo_draft_v3.pdf) and a sample latency evidence CSV from a comparable migration we ran (latency_evidence_20261101.csv).

Next steps: if this looks acceptable we can:
1) Lock the numbers and carveout language into the addendum.
2) Schedule a short technical pre-migration runbook review with your SREs.
3) Agree on a post-migration evidence checklist (we already included a template in the attached draft).

Happy to discuss adjustments — e.g., narrower p95 if you can accept a larger p50 or stronger cache-warming commitments.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
(Attachment: greenbank_slo_draft_v3.pdf; latency_evidence_20261101.csv)

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T11:24:00-08:00
Subject: internal: GreenBank SLO concession / evidence ask

Karthik / Neha — quick internal thread so procurement and engineering expectations line up. Daniel asked for firm tenant-level p50/p95 and a migration carveout. My proposed public-facing numbers above are p50 60ms / p95 320ms with a 3% transient tolerance for up to 72 hours if pre-notified.

Questions for engineering (Karthik):
- Is 320ms p95 at tenant level (hosted, global) realistic with our current caching + autoscale defaults? Any caveats for large-batched embedding calls?
- If we agree the carveout, what evidence package can we provide? Karthik suggested: prefix/KV cache warm logs, autoscale events, request traces aligned to their migration window.

Procurement (Neha):
- Is 72 hours reasonable from a legal/procurement perspective as a timebox? They want it codified as a "timebound tolerance" (no credits if pre-notified and within the tolerance). We need to ensure this doesn't create an open-ended credit exemption.

Quick bullets from me:
- Recommend accepting the 72-hour box but require GreenBank to provide exact runbook times and sign the addendum.
- We commit to a post-migration analysis within 5 business days and to provide metric correlation evidence (we'll redact any customer PII).

Karthik — can you confirm the instrumentation set we can promise and whether we need an internal escalated ops play during the window? If so, we'll include that as a prerequisite for the carveout.

Thanks,
Lauren

-- quoted for context --
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <dpark@greenbank.com>
Subject: Re: Latency commitments + migration carveouts

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-08T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: internal: GreenBank SLO concession / evidence ask

Lauren / Neha — quick notes from infra perspective: 

- Feasibility: p95 320ms is achievable for typical request sizes (chat/text-gen with <= 512 tokens). For very large sequences or large embedding batches p95 can creep higher; we should call that out in the addendum as "model/sequence-dependent exceptions" and require GreenBank to share typical payload sizes.

- Instrumentation we can commit to:
  * Per-tenant per-route 1-minute latency histograms (retained 30 days)
  * Cache warm events and KV cache hit-rate snapshots during the specified window
  * Autoscaler event logs and GPU pool utilization metrics correlated to timestamps
  * Trace IDs for any request samples we surface in the evidence package (we'll redact user content).

- Operational caveat: to offer the 3% transient tolerance we need a pre-migration checklist: pre-warm caches for the top 1,000 prefixes, enable burst capacity for the tenant for the duration, and a 2-hour canary ramp before cutover. If those steps aren't performed we should not offer the tolerance.

I'll draft the technical checklist items we need to include in the SLO addendum.

— Karthik

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Park <dpark@greenbank.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-09T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Latency commitments + migration carveouts — agreed draft and next steps

Daniel — thanks for the quick turn. Per internal alignment, Redwood can proceed with the following addendum text (summary):

1) Tenant-level SLO commitments (GreenBank-prod): p50 <= 60 ms; p95 <= 320 ms. These targets apply to typical request payload sizes (<=512 tokens). Larger sequences and bulk embedding jobs are scoped as "model/sequence-dependent" and are excluded from baseline latency commitments unless explicitly listed.

2) Measurement: 1-minute latency buckets; hourly rolling-window percentiles calculated from the last 60 buckets; 24-hour rolling window for breach detection; 30-day lookback for trend analysis. Reports: daily automated SLO report + weekly executive summary.

3) Migration carveout (timeboxed tolerance):
   - GreenBank provides 72-hour pre-notice with start/end timestamps.
   - Provided Redwood's pre-migration checklist is satisfied (pre-warm top prefixes, enable burst pool, perform 2-hour canary ramp), Redwood will allow up to 3% p95 exceedance during the 72-hour window without SLA credit.
   - GreenBank will supply migration traces/timestamps; Redwood will produce a post-migration correlation report within 5 business days.

4) Evidence & exclusions: cache warming logs, autoscale events, and request traces will be part of the evidence bundle. Scheduled maintenance windows and force majeure events remain carveouts per the base SLA.

Next steps:
- Please confirm you accept the above summary and we'll attach it as an addendum to the MSA.
- Agree a date for the runbook review (30–45 minute call) — we suggest Nov 18 or Nov 19.
- Signoff path: once GreenBank confirms, we'll produce a DocuSign-ready addendum and a pre-migration checklist doc in the shared Drive.

If you want a tighter p95 target we can discuss trading some of our burst capacity for a lower p95, but that will change pricing.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
